content: Truth conquers by itself; opinion by foreign aids.
author: Epictetus
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Living in pretense takes an enormous amount of mental energy. When you constantly manage impressions to please others, you end up feeling like an imposter in your own skin.

Epictetus understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Honesty with yourself can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is the only ground upon which a real life can be built. When you stop lying to yourself about your feelings, your energy is immediately freed up.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
